title: wiki_index.json (contract C11, index_version 1)
description: Search and graph index of the published wiki, written by the site generator (step 9) into the mkdocs docs dir so that it is copied into site/ and served as a static asset at /<config.mcp.index_file>. Read by the MCP Worker (worker/src). Plain data: no HTML, no scores, no normalised text.

index_version.description: Shape version; equals config.json mcp.index_version. Bump both together on a breaking change.

generated_at.description: When step 9 wrote the index (UTC, ISO 8601 with offset).

disclaimer.description: The site's warning in one markdown line (the line every markdown twin of a page opens with): AI-generated from group conversations, unverified, no professional advice, with a link to the terms. get_page opens every page body with it.

labels.description: Every label of the plan (C7 labels), keyed by label id.

pages.description: Every published page, in site navigation order (the order of the mkdocs nav).

day.description: YYYY-MM-DD, an ISO datetime, or null when the page has no claims.

url.description: Site-relative URL exactly as mkdocs publishes the page (use_directory_urls: 'colombia/'; the home page is '').

labels.description: Label ids of the page (front matter labels[].id); each must be a key of the top-level labels.

path.description: Front matter path: section ancestors from the root to the parent, [] for a top-level page.

related.description: Front matter related, with slug renamed to id; only ids of published pages.

out_links.description: Distinct targets of [[page_id|text]] links in the body (utils.wiki_links.find_wiki_links, kind 'page'), in order of first appearance, only published pages, never the page itself. In-links are derived by the Worker.

claims.description: Front matter claims statistics, copied as is.

status.description: Front matter status, only when draft or deprecated.

text.description: The page body markdown (C9 body_md) without front matter, wiki links kept in their [[page_id|text]] / [[label:id|text]] form.
